response.sql: SELECT m.college, SUM(i.amount) AS total_income, CAST(SUM(i.amount) AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM income) AS fraction_of_total FROM income i JOIN member mem ON i.link_to_member = mem.member_id JOIN major m ON mem.link_to_major = m.major_id GROUP BY m.college

assumptions.assumption: The fraction's denominator is the total of all income records (including any with no member or no major), not just the income that links to a college. Income without a member or major is excluded from the college rows, so the fractions may sum to less than 1.
Inner joins are used, so colleges with no linked income are not shown, and income records without a member or major do not appear in any college row.
'Without rounding' means the fraction is returned as a raw floating-point value, with no ROUND applied.

alternatives.interpretation: The fraction is relative to the total income that links to a college (the sum of the college totals), so the fractions sum to 1.
alternatives.sql: SELECT m.college, SUM(i.amount) AS total_income, CAST(SUM(i.amount) AS REAL) / SUM(SUM(i.amount)) OVER () AS fraction_of_total FROM income i JOIN member mem ON i.link_to_member = mem.member_id JOIN major m ON mem.link_to_major = m.major_id GROUP BY m.college
